name: Obernberg am Brenner
kurzbeschreibung: Highest-lying municipality in the Wipptal with untouched Alpine nature and the source of the Sill river.
beschreibung:
Overview

Obernberg am Brenner is situated in an unspoilt southwestern side valley of the Wipp Valley in the Tyrolean district of Innsbruck-Land, about 35 kilometres south of Innsbruck at an altitude of 1,390 metres near the main alpine ridge. This tranquil mountain municipality has around 400 residents and covers an alpine high valley of 38.6 square kilometres bordering South Tyrol. As an official member of the prestigious Mountaineering Villages initiative of the Alpine Clubs, Obernberg is dedicated to gentle, sustainable tourism. You will find no mega-resorts or cable car networks here; instead, listed wooden farmsteads in classic Tyrolean architectural style, open larch meadows, and majestic mountain vistas define the valley. The scenery is crowned by the imposing limestone walls of the Tribulaun massif, most notably the Obernberger Tribulaun (2,780 m), offering dramatic contrasts against the gentle alpine ridges.

History

Human settlement in the Obernberg Valley began in prehistoric times, as early travellers crossed the Sandjoch pass into South Tyrol during the Bronze and Iron Ages. The valley was first documented around 1305 under the name Obernperch. For centuries, the local population sustained itself through alpine farming, livestock rearing, and mule-track trade across the mountain passes. Artistically, Obernberg preserves a true gem of Tyrolean Rococo: the Parish Church of St. Nicholas, built around 1760 to designs by the famed Tyrolean master priest Franz de Paula Penz. The interior features exquisite Rococo stucco work by Anton Gigl from Wessobrunn and vibrant ceiling frescoes by court painter Christoph Anton Mayr. Another iconic sight is the lake chapel Maria am See on the shores of Lake Obernberg, built in 1935 on the site of an earlier shrine and today one of the most photographed motifs in Tyrol.

Getting There

Reaching Obernberg am Brenner is straightforward via the Brenner transport corridor. By car, leave the Brenner Autobahn A13 at the Matrei am Brenner or Nösslach exit, or travel along the toll-free Brenner federal road B182 to Gries am Brenner. From Gries, take the well-maintained Obernberg provincial road L38, winding up the valley in approximately ten minutes to the trailhead car park at Waldesruh. Rail passengers travel along the Brenner railway line by ÖBB trains to Steinach am Brenner or Gries am Brenner stations. Connecting regional bus services operated by Verkehrsverbund Tirol (VVT) depart regularly from the stations, carrying guests to Obernberg in about 15 to 20 minutes. With the local guest card, all public regional buses and local trains throughout the Wipp Valley are completely free of charge.

Tips

The undisputed natural highlight of the valley is the protected nature reserve of Lake Obernberg at 1,590 metres above sea level. This crystal-clear mountain lake is famous for its iridescent turquoise and emerald hues fed by subterranean springs. To preserve the rare stonewort algae and fragile aquatic ecosystem, swimming and boating are strictly prohibited. A scenic walking loop circles both parts of the lake, leading across a wooden bridge to the chapel Maria am See perched on a wooded peninsula. Mountaineers can tackle demanding climbs up the Obernberger Tribulaun or scenic ridge hikes across the Sandjoch. In winter, the valley becomes a haven for ski touring enthusiasts, snowshoers, and sledging fans who enjoy the popular natural toboggan run at Waldesruh.
